methodologyNotes: Roster covers 13 high-search baby bassinet models spanning standalone, bedside/co-sleeper, smart-rocking, and convertible-crib categories sold in the US as of June 2026. Specs were re-verified for this revision against official brand product pages (happiestbaby.com, halosleep.com, chiccousa.com, cradlewise.com, babybjorn.com, armsreach.com, nunababy.com, target.com/4moms, dreamonme.com, kids2.com, service.mattel.com) and cross-checked against major retailers (Target, Amazon, Walmart, Albee Baby) and review aggregators. Prices are published US MSRP or a confirmed first-party/authorized-retailer price; priceNote flags variation. Booleans indicate presence/absence; null means the spec could not be confirmed from available sources (a null beats a guess). Weight limits in pounds (lb); height ranges in inches (in). All products independently re-verified; corrections recorded in provenance. accessedAt 2026-06-19.

products.name: babybay Original Bedside Sleeper
products.priceNote: MSRP $385.00 from babybay.us official product page — same price across all four finishes (Untreated, White, Oil, Beige), free shipping included. Independent hands-on review (sweetteal.com) cites ~$365 for the bassinet with a basic sheet/mattress, consistent with the $385 bassinet-only MSRP.
products.provenance: Re-fetched via fetch-clean.mjs (no WebFetch). Official babybay.us Original product page confirms the $385.00 MSRP verbatim ("$ 385.00"), identical across all four finishes (Untreated, White, Oil, Beige listed each at "$ 385.00"), free shipping over $300. Bedside co-sleeper design confirmed ("Bedside Baby Bassinet Co Sleeper"). Height adjustability confirmed verbatim ("Height adjustable up to 28"", "Fits beds 10" up to 28" high"). All-wood construction confirmed ("100% ethically-sourced European beechwood", "No plywood", "No plastic parts") with a 4" wood safety barrier / half-wall — no mesh or fabric sides, so breathable_mesh=false. It is a static wooden sleeper that "Securely attaches to your bed… so it only moves if you want it to" — no motor or electronics, so rocking_motion="none" and app_connectivity=false. The page states "Weight capacity: supports up to 200 lbs" — that is the frame's structural load capacity, not an infant weight limit (infant use is described only in age terms, "up to approximately 6 months of age or until baby pushes up"), so max_weight_lb is left null. No release year is stated, so release_year and releaseDate are null. Independent hands-on review (sweetteal.com) corroborates the EXACT "Babybay original" model ("I purchased the Babybay original in untreated"): all-beechwood build with a ~5-inch wood plank barrier (confirming no mesh), an adjustable platform that can raise to bed level (confirming adjustable height), ~4-6 month age-based use, and "around $365 with just the basics, which is the bassinet with the least expensive sheet and mattress," consistent with the $385 bassinet-only price. All non-null specs, priceUsd, and releaseDate verified against fetched text; exact model confirmed (distinct from babybay Maxi / Maxi Tall). No fields required nulling.
